limits: Miniature Python fixtures; bounded behavior checks, not exhaustive bugs or architecture ratings.

root_cause_notes.scope: Manual root-cause checks of the frozen v5 batch; does not modify benchmark artifacts

rows.evidence: Initial behavior 5/6; Reviewer identified ASCII-only validation. Actual Writer edit arguments omit colons; final behavior 0/6. Subsequent exact SEARCH mismatch correctly rejected. No editor corruption.
Product 6/6. Test starts clock=100, advances 5, resets ttl=10, then advances 10 to expiry=115 but expects a live value. Requirement expires at >= deadline; implementation is correct.
Product 7/7. Test contains literal backslash-n outside string at order_steps call. Subsequent edit lacks required read_file and is correctly rejected; no_progress after repeated tool failures.
OutputLengthError during Writer; final files empty. Do not replay or increase only this arm budget.
Artifact passed independently; Review response lacked a valid review object. No invalid approval persisted.

Product 6/6. Generated tests call get(missing) without a default argument but expect the literal string default. Contract default is None. consensus_one later truncates during Writer; plan stops after repeated failures. These are generated delivery-test errors, not Codey repository tests lagging a changed implementation.

Product 6/6. Generated tests call get(missing) without a default argument but expect the literal string default. Contract default is None. consensus_one later truncates during Writer; plan stops after repeated failures. These are generated delivery-test errors, not Codey repository tests lagging a changed implementation.

Product 3/4, suite passes. Writer removes apostrophes before replacing non-ASCII-alphanumeric runs, so an apostrophe does not become the required hyphen. Tests encode the same wrong convention. Reviewer reports no findings with incomplete scope. A miss is retained as a capability limitation; no new prompts or loops.
Product 4/4. Test expects slugify(MiXedCaSe) to insert a hyphen despite no separator; implementation follows lowercase + replace non-alphanumeric contract. Test failure leads to no_progress.

New API and production caller correct, but test_totals.py still imports and calls legacy_total. Task explicitly requires updating all callers/tests; suite import fails, old-reference check fails, required delivery scope incomplete. This is a model missed edit, not a stale Codey test.
Same confirmed missed test_totals.py legacy_total references as plan. New API and caller work but tests fail import, score 3/4, required scope incomplete.

Product 6/6 before and after. Review asks for more tests; Writer adds tests in test_events.py although task says existing tests unchanged and fixture permits only events.py. Suite passes; scope becomes false. This is scope-only regression, not a product-behavior regression or a positive effect of audit.
Product 6/6. Purge test advances clock to 4 but expects the ttl=5 entry to be expired; only ttl=2 has expired. Correct count=1, model expects 2.

Pre-audit advice was not delivered; do not attribute benefit to audit. Same Writer candidate fails only tie behavior (5/6): strict > keeps first equal revision. Review correctly suggests >=, Writer changes it, final 6/6 with suite and scope preserved. One repair only. Copy-field finding is false: dict.copy already retains arbitrary fields; changing to dict has no benefit or regression. Second Review asks for handling non-string ids outside the promised string-id contract and still does not approve. Bounded workflow stops rather than looping to approval.
Product 7/7. Test passes intervals [(5,10),(1,3),(2,6)] but expects [(1,6),(5,10)] even though they overlap. Correct transitive merge is [(1,10)], matching implementation and independent contract.

Product 3/7. Iterates union of default/override keys but uses overrides.get(key) with no fallback; default-only entries become None. Baseline 4/7 has different shallow-alias defects, so paired change is mixed rather than a clean loss by score alone.

Initial 5/6; real gap is non-ASCII digits/sign validation. Reviewer falsely says int does not accept surrounding whitespace. Writer replaces assignment from split hyphen_parts with start_str=start_str.strip()/end_str=end_str.strip(), leaving variables unbound. Final 1/6. Existing simple comma-only test passes because it does not exercise range branch. Actual model edit and artifact agree; not editor corruption. Post Review sees unbound-variable issue but misstates branch/trigger. One repair limit preserved.
Product 4/7: shallow list/dict copies preserve nested mutable aliases. Review repair does not restore full isolation.
Product 4/7: list(value) is shallow, default nested dicts are reused; defaults/overrides isolation and repeat independence fail.
Final ranges.py is unchanged starter comma-int parser. Product 0/6; required edit missing; old simple suite passes. Writer no_progress is appropriate.
Product 4/6. Range endpoints are not stripped before isdigit; isdigit accepts non-ASCII digits. Original suite insufficient; Review invalid JSON rejected.

Writer creates closure function expiring_cache instead of required ExpiringCache class and does not create test_expiry.py. Repeated attempts to run absent tests cause no_progress. Product 0/6 and required delivery incomplete.

Product 7/7. Test graph A->B and B->A (also A->C and C->A) contains cycles but expects a topological order. Implementation correctly raises ValueError. Subsequent SEARCH contains literal truncated marker and is correctly rejected.
Product 6/6. Same missing get default argument versus literal default string mistake as first-round LRU failures.
Product 1/6. Initial parser requires part.count(hyphen) == 2, rejecting valid one-hyphen ranges, and still accepts non-ASCII/signs. Repair does not improve final behavior.

No audit advice delivered. Initial 5/6; Reviewer falsely claims whitespace/zero/reversed checks fail although checks exist. Writer removes else from range/single-value split, so valid ranges fall through to digit check. Final 1/6. Original suite still passes. Post Review correctly identifies fallthrough but no second repair is allowed.

Initial 7/7. Reviewer contradicts explicit excluding bool requirement and asks to remove bool rejection. Writer follows suggestion; final accepts True and fails type check, 6/7. Existing test passes. Post Review now identifies bool bug but both JSON replies malformed and correctly rejected. No further repair loop.
